risks: No participants; the risk is an overconfident summary that leads to unsafe early discharge, or an overcautious one that keeps the unit crowded.
data: No personal data; search strategy, screening log and extraction sheet archived with the report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: age over 75, kidney disease, sex (atypical presentations in women) and language barriers can affect both rule-out yield and safety. The review reports results by age and kidney function where available, notes studies that excluded these groups, and asks the committee to monitor time saved for older patients.
effectiveness: The review is useful if the committee can see safety, the likely local yield and the practical failure points before approving the change.
efficiency: Existing librarian and clinician time only.
costs: About ten librarian hours and 12 reviewer days within existing roles.
partnerships: Laboratory director, emergency nursing lead, a cardiology registrar and two patient partners from the cardiac patient group.
rebPath: No research ethics review is required for a review of published data; any later local evaluation of the pathway would be screened as quality improvement.
limitations: Single screening with a 20 percent check, English only, and no author contact.
summary: Review of published data with an equity focus on age, kidney disease and sex.
